# brig sandbox run

Run a command in a new sandbox, with files in and out, and delete it

## Synopsis

```text
brig sandbox run [VM] (--image IMG | --template T) [flags] -- COMMAND [ARG...]
```

## Description

Run a command in a sandbox of its own: create the sandbox, copy files into
it, run the command, copy files out and delete the sandbox. Without VM, the
VM is the one that [`brig use`](brig-use.md) selected.

The sandbox is called run-\<time\>-\<random\>, or --name. It has the providers
that --provider names and no others, and the policy --policy, or else the
VM's default sandbox policy. With --image, brig first copies the image from
the host's Podman into the VM if the VM lacks it.

--upload SRC[:DIR] copies the host file or directory SRC into the sandbox
directory DIR, which is relative to /sandbox and is /sandbox itself by
default. As openshell does, it leaves out what .gitignore names, unless
--upload-all. --download PATH[:DEST] copies the sandbox's PATH, relative to
/sandbox, to the host's DEST, by default PATH's base name in the current
directory. Downloads happen also when the command fails.

The command's standard output and error are brig's, and brig exits with the
command's exit status, 124 if --timeout stopped it. brig's own failures exit
with the statuses that brig --help lists, and Ctrl-C deletes the sandbox and
exits with 130 (143 for SIGTERM). With --stdin, the command gets brig's
standard input, up to 960 KiB; otherwise it gets none.

--keep failed keeps the sandbox when the command or brig fails, --keep always
keeps it anyway. A kept sandbox carries the labels brig.dev/run and
brig.dev/expires, and [`brig sandbox clean`](brig-sandbox-clean.md) --runs deletes it once it expires:
a day after the run started, or with --timeout, an hour past the timeout.

--result FILE writes a JSON record of the run: its sandbox, exit status,
transfers and the requests that the policy denied, by host and binary.
--dry-run prints the openshell commands that the run amounts to.

## Examples

```sh
brig sandbox run dev --image localhost/pi-agent:2026-10-08 --upload ./task \
  --download task/out --result run.json -- make -C task
brig sandbox run --template claude --provider claude-code --timeout 30m \
  --keep failed --upload ./repo --workdir repo -- claude -p "fix the tests"
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--download stringArray` | copy the sandbox's PATH, relative to /sandbox, to the host's DEST after the command: PATH[:DEST] (repeatable) |
| `--dry-run` | print the openshell commands that the run amounts to, and do nothing |
| `--env stringArray` | set a non-secret environment variable for the command: KEY=VALUE (repeatable); attach a provider for secrets |
| `--image string` | create the sandbox from this container image |
| `--keep string` | keep the sandbox: never, failed or always (default `never`) |
| `--name string` | name the sandbox (default: run-\<time\>-\<random\>) |
| `--policy string` | the sandbox's policy file (default: the VM's default sandbox policy) |
| `--provider stringArray` | attach this provider (repeatable) |
| `--result string` | write a JSON record of the run to this file |
| `--start` | start the VM if it is stopped |
| `-i, --stdin` | pass standard input to the command, up to 960 KiB |
| `--template string` | create the sandbox from this sandbox template of the gateway |
| `--timeout duration` | stop the command after this long, e.g. 30m, and exit with 124 (default: no limit) |
| `--upload stringArray` | copy host file or directory SRC into sandbox directory DIR, relative to /sandbox, before the command: SRC[:DIR] (repeatable) |
| `--upload-all` | upload what .gitignore names too |
| `--workdir string` | run the command in this directory of the sandbox |
| `-w, --workspace string` | the workspace of the gateway to work in (default: $BRIG\_WORKSPACE, else default) |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
